titulo: Prepositions and crase: the grave accent «à»: Crase: when «a» becomes «à»

aula.titulo: Prepositions and crase: the grave accent «à»
aula.objetivo: Choose the preposition that each common verb requires (often different from English), write the grave accent «à» correctly with a simple two-step test, and use the prepositions of time and place in both the written and the spoken norm.

blocos.titulo: Crase: the grave accent and a simple test
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: crase is the fusion of two «a»: the preposition «a» (to, at) plus the feminine article «a» (or the first «a» of «aquele, aquela, aquilo»). It is written «à». You do not hear a different sound; it is a spelling rule, and you need it when you write. Example: «Vou a + a escola» becomes «Vou à escola». STEP 2: both conditions must be true: (1) the verb or noun asks for the preposition «a» (ir a, chegar a, dar a, entregar a, assistir a, fiel a...); and (2) the next word is feminine and takes the article «a» («a escola», «a feira», «a Bahia»). If one is missing, there is no accent. STEP 3: the test. Replace the feminine word by a masculine one: if you would say «ao», the feminine takes «à»: «Vou ao mercado» → «Vou à feira». For place names use the second test: say «volto de...». If you say «volto DA Bahia», write «vou À Bahia». If you say «volto DE Portugal», write «vou A Portugal». STEP 4: never before masculine words («a pé», «a cavalo»), verbs («começar a estudar»), personal pronouns («a ele», «a você», «a mim»), the indefinite article («dei o livro a uma amiga»), plurals without article («a festas»), or between repeated words («cara a cara», «passo a passo»). Also «casa» alone: «cheguei a casa» (no article), but with a complement, «cheguei à casa de Maria». STEP 5: always with the fixed feminine expressions («à direita, à esquerda, às vezes, à vista, à noite, à tarde, à vontade») and with hours: «às oito horas», «à uma hora», «das nove às cinco». For days, use «de segunda a sexta» (no article, no accent). STEP 6: a practical shortcut for speakers: when you doubt, use «para»: «Vou para a Bahia», «Vou para a escola». This is correct and has no accent. In speech Brazilians often say «vou pra escola» or «vou na escola», so crase matters mostly in writing.
blocos.comparacao: English has no equivalent. Think of it as a spelling note: the accent says «to + the» in one letter, like the English «at the» contracting to a single sound in fast speech. In careful writing, a missing accent is one of the most visible errors of Portuguese writers, including Brazilians.

linhas.place: a Bahia, a França, a Argentina
o Brasil, o Peru, o Rio de Janeiro

erros.motivo: Preposition «a» + article «a»: test with «vou ao colégio».
Before a verb there is no article, so no crase.
Personal pronouns such as «ele» do not take the article.
In «de... a...» there is no article, so no accent.

blocos.enunciado: Write on paper six short sentences about places you will go this week: a pharmacy, a market, the bank, a friend's house, Bahia, Portugal. For each, run the test aloud («Vou ao mercado» / «Volto da Bahia») and decide if you write «a» or «à». Then read the sentences aloud with «para» instead of «a», as in everyday speech.
Say aloud five sentences with «ir a» or «ir para» and a place (the bank, the market, the school). Notice that you used «a» + the article. This is the group where crase happens.
